item.text:
## Xi Jinping in 2024: `1B.6` nonproliferation discipline

Best read: **China under Xi publicly supported nonproliferation, export control, and denuclearization diplomacy in 2024, but there was also clear evidence of PRC-based procurement support for DPRK programs and of China shielding Iran from pressure rather than pressing hard against proliferation.** I did **not** find direct 2024 evidence that Xi personally blocked a specific ally/proxy/client proliferation push because it conflicted with short-term interests.

| Direction | Title | Publisher | Date | Recoverable page URL | Claim-level summary | QIDs |
|---|---|---:|---|---|---|---|
| Supports `1B.6` | [China's Non-Proliferation Policy and Measures](https://www.mfa.gov.cn/eng/wjb/zzjg_663340/jks_665232/kjlc_665236/fkswt_665240/202406/t20240606_11405135.html) | PRC Ministry of Foreign Affairs | 2024-06-06 | https://www.mfa.gov.cn/eng/wjb/zzjg_663340/jks_665232/kjlc_665236/fkswt_665240/202406/t20240606_11405135.html | China said it opposes WMD proliferation, has a legal and export-control system covering nuclear and missile-related items, and promotes peaceful resolution of the Korean Peninsula and Iran nuclear issues. This is the clearest broad nonproliferation-policy support. | `1B.6`, `1B.4`, `1B.1` |
| Supports `1B.6` | [Statement by H.E. Ambassador Cheng Jingye ... General Debate of the 61st Session of UNGA First Committee](https://www.mfa.gov.cn/eng/wjb/zzjg_663340/jks_665232/kjfywj_665252/202406/t20240606_11405245.html) | PRC Ministry of Foreign Affairs | 2024-06-06 | https://www.mfa.gov.cn/eng/wjb/zzjg_663340/jks_665232/kjfywj_665252/202406/t20240606_11405245.html | China backed denuclearization of the Korean Peninsula and said it was opposed to proliferation of nuclear weapons on the Iranian file, while stressing diplomacy and arms-control mechanisms. This supports resistance to proliferation in official policy terms. | `1B.6`, `1B.4` |
| Supports `1B.6` | [Position Paper of the People's Republic of China For the 77th Session of the United Nations General Assembly](https://www.mfa.gov.cn/mfa_eng/zy/wjzc/202405/t20240531_11367524.html) | PRC Ministry of Foreign Affairs | 2024-05-31 | https://www.mfa.gov.cn/mfa_eng/zy/wjzc/202405/t20240531_11367524.html | China said it firmly opposes WMD proliferation and criticized AUKUS nuclear-submarine cooperation as undermining the NPT. That is direct nonproliferation signaling, though not a specific ally/proxy test. | `1B.6`, `1B.4` |
| Supports `1B.6` | [All Parties Reiterate to Fully and Effectively Implement the JCPOA on the Iranian Nuclear Issue](https://www.mfa.gov.cn/eng/wjb/zzjg_663340/xybfs_663590/xwlb_663592/202406/t20240606_11387067.html) | PRC Ministry of Foreign Affairs | 2024-06-06 | https://www.mfa.gov.cn/eng/wjb/zzjg_663340/xybfs_663590/xwlb_663592/202406/t20240606_11387067.html | China backed full JCPOA implementation and opposed dispute-escalation, which is consistent with resisting further Iranian nuclear advancement through diplomacy. The evidence is pro-restraint, not enforcement-heavy. | `1B.6`, `1B.4` |
| Cuts against `1B.6` | [Treasury Targets PRC-based Procurement Network Supporting DPRK Ballistic Missile and Space Programs](https://home.treasury.gov/news/press-releases/jy2482) | U.S. Department of the Treasury | 2024-07-24 | https://home.treasury.gov/news/press-releases/jy2482 | Treasury sanctioned a PRC-based network for procuring items that supported DPRK ballistic missile and space programs. This is strong evidence that Chinese-based actors still enabled proliferation despite official policy. | `1B.6`, `1B.1` |
| Cuts against `1B.6` | [Chinese envoy: Pressure and power politics are not diplomacy, confrontation will not solve the Iran nuclear issue](https://www.mfa.gov.cn/eng/xw/zwbd/202412/t20241205_11538812.html) | PRC Ministry of Foreign Affairs | 2024-11-22 | https://www.mfa.gov.cn/eng/xw/zwbd/202412/t20241205_11538812.html | China voted against an IAEA resolution that would have increased pressure on Iran, arguing for diplomacy instead. That can be read as reluctance to confront a proliferating partner, even if framed as anti-escalatory. | `1B.6`, `1B.4` |

### Synthesis

- **Best support:** Xi-era Chinese policy in 2024 strongly endorsed nonproliferation, denuclearization, export control, and diplomatic settlement of Iran and DPRK nuclear issues.
- **Best counterevidence:** PRC-based procurement networks still aided DPRK missile programs, and China resisted pressure on Iran at the IAEA.
- **Bottom line for `1B.6`:** **mixed, with better rhetoric than enforcement.** The record supports nonproliferation as state doctrine, but shows incomplete resistance when Chinese interests favored softer handling of Iran or tolerated PRC-linked procurement networks.

### Search gap

I did **not** find direct 2024 evidence that Xi personally:
- overrode an ally/proxy/client to stop proliferation,
- punished a domestic faction specifically for pushing proliferation,
- or publicly took a hard line against a proliferation channel when it was politically convenient.

So the evidence is mostly **policy-level and indirect**, not a clean personal intervention record.
